big_case.notes: Significant Solicitor General emergency application resulting in a 6-page published per curiam opinion clarifying that major-questions challenges to agency action remain statutory rather than constitutional claims under Dalton v. Specter for purposes of IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(A)'s jurisdiction strip, and unblocking over 300 miles of southern-border barrier construction.

leakage.notes: Forward prediction run on 2026-10-23 with no external retrieval beyond reading the provisioned event files, application.txt, and metrics/statpack.md.

central_claims.basis: On November 9, 2026 (within the predicted 'first half of November 2026' window), the Court referred the application to the full Court and granted a stay pending the filing and disposition of a certiorari petition without summarily reversing (pp. 1, 5-6).
central_claims.claim: The Court will refer the application to the full Court and grant a stay pending the timely filing and disposition of a petition for a writ of certiorari, while declining to grant certiorari and summarily reverse.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion rested primarily on IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(A) and Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. 462, 472-473 (1994), holding that the district court likely lacked jurisdiction because respondents' major-questions claim was statutory rather than constitutional (pp. 3-5).
central_claims.claim: The primary ground is IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(A)'s bar on non-constitutional claims: under Dalton v. Specter, a major-questions argument is a claim that the Secretary exceeded statutory authority, not a constitutional claim, so the district court likely lacked jurisdiction.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion cited § 102(c)(2)(C)'s direct-certiorari review mechanism and Trump v. Sierra Club, 588 U.S. 930 (2019), in holding that the Government satisfied the stay factors and balance of equities (pp. 2, 5).
central_claims.claim: Review lies only by direct certiorari to the Supreme Court under IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(C), satisfying the cert-worthiness prong, and the balance of equities on border-barrier construction follows Trump v. Sierra Club (2019).

central_claims.basis: Instead of a short unreasoned order with two or three noted dissents, the Court issued a 6-page reasoned per curiam opinion and only Justice Jackson noted that she would deny the application (pp. 1-6).
central_claims.claim: The disposition will likely be a short unsigned order without a full per curiam opinion, accompanied by two or three noted dissents from Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson.
